Thompson-Epstein classification: 1

A patient sustains posterior hip dislocation after a dashboard injury. Imaging reveals no substantial acetabular fracture and only a tiny insignificant posterior rim fragment. Which Thompson-Epstein grade best describes the associated bony injury?

  1. Thompson-Epstein I
  2. Thompson-Epstein II
  3. Thompson-Epstein III
  4. Thompson-Epstein IV
  5. Thompson-Epstein V
Answer and explanation

Thompson-Epstein I

Posterior hip dislocation has no significant acetabular fracture or only a minor fragment.

Option explanations

Thompson-Epstein I: Posterior hip dislocation has no significant acetabular fracture or only a minor fragment.

Thompson-Epstein II: Posterior dislocation accompanies a single large posterior acetabular wall fragment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Thompson-Epstein III: Posterior dislocation accompanies a comminuted posterior acetabular wall fracture. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Thompson-Epstein IV: Posterior dislocation is associated with fracture of the acetabular floor. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Thompson-Epstein V: Posterior dislocation is associated with femoral head fracture. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
